timingSemantics.gpuMs: legacy alias of queueSpanGpuMs; retained for report compatibility
timingSemantics.queueSpanGpuMs: GPU timestamp span from a marker submitted before the async pass callback until a marker submitted after it returns; includes queued GPU work and may include GPU-idle time caused by host waits before the ending marker is submitted
timingSemantics.commandGpuMs: sum of explicitly bracketed command-buffer submissions made through performanceTimingScope.submit(); each start/work/end sequence is submitted atomically to the queue and excludes host gaps between submit calls
timingSemantics.hostWaitMs: explicit host-side waits recorded through performanceTimingScope.recordHostWait()/measureHostWait(); never a GPU-time substitute
timingSemantics.readbackMapLatencyMs: wall-clock latency of SM-500 timestamp readback mapAsync; diagnostic transport latency, not GPU execution time

stages.reason: Canonical opaque/material ownership is the stable scene input for every later forward pass.
Water refracts the resolved opaque scene and must reject fragments hidden by nearer canonical ownership.
Receiver-only Fine Grass stays in the lit world and cannot become a post/UI overlay.
Background-classified rooted foliage stays behind representative actors/props using canonical depth plus the SM-401 classifier.
Ordinary transparent world sprites are rejected behind opaque ownership without stealing depth.
World glow sprites share canonical depth policy but retain additive compatibility blending.
Only foliage explicitly classified in front may cross the actor/prop surface; the ordering decision is data, not submission order.
Bloom/grade or raw/debug copy transforms the complete lit world once; bypass changes the operation, not layer semantics.
Compatibility shader FX intentionally remain after final world post so feedback intensity/readability is not regraded.
Top glow feedback bypasses world depth and remains above post-effects.
Top alpha sprites preserve the compatibility ordering after top glows.
The active objective marker remains readable above top sprites.
Guide feedback is the final gameplay readability layer, matching the accepted compatibility path.
Debug ordering visualization and external UI/present happen after gameplay layers and are never implicit renderer ordering.
